applies_why: The judge text resolves a collision over Matthew 1:20 between the challenger's covenant-presence chain in [DR3] and the defender's physical-source chain in [CR2] and [CR3], so the rule governs that collision.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'weighs chain against chain by footing': one reading requires the judge to set out and compare the chains' support; the other permits a bare underdetermination label without such comparison. I used the first because the rule expressly requires chain-against-chain footing rather than a verse-level or bare-opposition test.
why: The judge text only notes that each side gave an answer and declares the point underdetermined; it does not weigh the challenger's and defender's chains against each other by footing as K-C requires.
